shots.phrase: Begin by framing Course Foundations and Scope as a question about inputs, decisions, and observable results.
Topics include search algorithms, logic, planning, machine learning, and applications from areas such as computer vision, robotics, and natural language processing.
List the givens before choosing a method, because an unstated assumption can change the conclusion.
Now define Prerequisites and Course Constraints precisely enough that another learner could test the definition.
Students cannot take and receive credit for this course if they have taken CSCI-630.
Separate the formal definition from an implementation detail, then identify what evidence would distinguish them.
With the foundation in place, examine how NIST AI Risk Management Framework operates in a concrete sequence.
Consider this worked case: Govern establishes policies, Map documents context and impacts, Measure analyzes risks, and Manage prioritizes responses.
The trace converts an abstract statement into an inspectable sequence.
Next, compare the choices involved in Risk Analysis Considerations and make the decision criteria explicit.
Consider this worked case: In a healthcare AI system, data quality and fairness are critical to ensure accurate diagnoses and equitable outcomes.
Using shared criteria turns a preference into a defensible technical choice.
Apply Monitoring and Context Changes to a worked situation instead of treating it as an isolated definition.
Monitoring continues after deployment because context and system behavior can change.
Work from the concrete inputs to the result, checking units, types, or invariants at each step.
Examine the tradeoffs in Machine Learning Workflow Overview, including what improves and what becomes more difficult.
Consider this worked case: Developing a spam filter involves cleaning email data, training a classifier, validating on unseen data, and testing performance.
Making the tradeoff visible prevents a local improvement from hiding a larger cost.
Stress-test the reasoning around Supervised and Unsupervised Methods with an edge case and identify which assumption controls the outcome.
Supervised methods learn a mapping from examples paired with target labels.
Change one assumption at a time and observe which part of the reasoning no longer holds.
Use Preprocessing and Leakage Prevention to diagnose a failure by separating symptoms, causes, and corrective action.
Preprocessing must be fitted only on permitted training data to avoid leakage.
Locate the first point where observed behavior diverges from expected behavior, then test the smallest plausible cause.
Connect Pipelines and Cross-Validation to the earlier ideas and explain how the pieces work as one system.
Cross-validation repeats training and validation across defined data splits.
Explain each connection explicitly and verify that information retains the same meaning across representations.
Finish with Evaluation Metrics and Hyperparameter Selection as a practical checklist that can guide a new analysis.
Evaluation metrics must match the task and the cost of different errors.
For each checklist item, record the evidence, the remaining uncertainty, and the next verification step.
